members.title: Initiative to amend Bank Company Act right step
members.lead: The Bank Company Act was amended in 2013, 2018 and 2023 during the tenure of the Awami League government, which was ousted from power through the July mass uprising. Those amendments catered to the interests of bank owners, leading to an increase in irregularities and corruption. The draft amendments to the banking law finalised by the incumbent BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party) government propose measures to curb family dominance and political influence in the banking sector. On the issue, Hossain Zillur Rahman, executive chairman of the Power and Participation Research Centre (PPRC), shared his views. . Reforming the banking sector has become essential now. The proposals put forward in the draft amendment to the Bank Company Act, 1991, are both appropriate and well-considered. We have seen how the influence of ministers, members of parliament (MPs), and family members of bank owners devastated the banking sector during the previous regime. The proposed provisions in the Bank Company Act amendment will reduce, at least to some extent, the grip of politically influential figures and dynastic control over bank boards of directors. For instance, the new draft recommends reducing the number of directors from the same family on a bank's board from three to two. . Similarly, the initiative to increase the number of independent directors is sound. Bank boards must include capable, honest, and qualified individuals as experts, which will serve the best interests of the banking sector. However, the concept of an independent director must not remain confined to the label "independent" alone; truly skilled and competent individuals must be appointed to these roles. There is also merit in the proposal to reduce the tenure of bank board members from 12 years to six years. members.title: ‘We are reforming the banking sector to break oligarchic control’
members.lead: The Bank Company Act was amended in 2013, 2018 and 2023 during the tenure of the Awami League government, which was ousted from power through the July mass uprising. Those amendments catered to the interests of bank owners, leading to an increase in irregularities and corruption. The draft amendments to the banking law finalised by the incumbent BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party) government propose measures to curb family dominance and political influence in the banking sector. On the issue, an interview was given by Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir , the Prime Minister’s Adviser on Finance and Planning. . The proposed amendments will reduce the number of directors from a single family on a bank’s board and limit members of the same family to a maximum of six consecutive years as directors, down from 12. How much will these changes help reduce the long-standing control of families and particular business groups over banks? Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir: The long-standing representation of multiple members of a single family on a bank’s board creates opportunities for family-centric control and influence. Such situations can undermine professional decision-making, transparency and accountability in banks. Therefore, these provisions need to be amended to establish a balance on the board and protect the institutional interests of banks. To this end, we have proposed reducing the maximum number of directors from a single family from three to two. We have also proposed that, instead of allowing one director each from two entities affiliated with or controlled by the same family, only one director be appointed to represent one such entity. Under the existing law, an individual can serve as a director of the same bank for 12 consecutive years. After a three-year break, they can return to the board.
